problem:
Given the functions $f(x),g(x)$ and $h(x)$ below, which of them has a jump discontinuity at $x=7?$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={\begin{aligned}2x-1, & x\le 7 \\ {x}^{2}-30, & x>7,\end{aligned} \\ g(x) & ={\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & x<7 \\ 5x+14, & x\ge 7,\end{aligned} \\ h(x) & ={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x-7}, & x<7 \\ \frac{1}{7}, & x\ge 7,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $f(x)$ below?

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+3, & x<1 \\ 1-{x}^{3}, & x\ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

- It has a jump discontinuity at $x=1.$
- It has a removable discontinuity at $x=1.$
- It's continuous at $x=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For $x=1,$ let's go through our continuity checklist:

- $f(1)=1-{1}^{3}=0$ exists $\,\,✓$

- Let's now check the left and right limits. We see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}({x}^{2}+3)=({1}^{2}+3)=4
$$

while 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}(1-{x}^{3})=(1-{1}^{3})=0.
$$

So both the left and right limits exist and are finite, but they are not equal. $\,\,\times $

Therefore, $f(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x=1.$

Hence, I is true, while II and III are false.
